content:
I mentioned in today's article about Siri AI on Apple Watch that there's still one change I hope Apple will make before watchOS 27 officially launches this month. This feature is a common muscle-memory operation that has existed for years, and I've been relying on it the entire summer.

In watchOS 27, double-clicking the digital crown can no longer quickly switch between different apps.

I wrote this morning:

I raised this issue back in July when Apple released the first public beta of watchOS 27, and I had also provided feedback to Apple in June.

For years, Apple Watch has had a hidden gesture feature that lets you quickly switch between two apps, or jump to the last-used app and watch face.

This is an operation I haven't consciously thought about for many years, yet I use it constantly.

In watchOS 27, single-clicking and double-clicking the digital crown brings up the Dynamic App Stack

watchOS 27 beta 1 removed this feature. It seems the reason is that Apple wants to heavily promote the new "Dynamic App Stack" feature in watchOS 27. Now, pressing the digital crown once displays the Siri app icon, along with five smart-suggested app icons, and an icon that lets you see the complete app stack.

The Dynamic App Stack is actually quite smooth to use. If the app you want to open is already in the suggested launch area, it is indeed very convenient.

But it simply cannot replace the reliable operation of double-clicking to quickly jump to another app. In watchOS 27, this action is completely impossible. In the watchOS 27 beta, double-clicking the digital crown produces exactly the same result as single-clicking it.

The old method allowed you to quickly jump back and forth between apps like Workout and Music.

As I mentioned before, Apple Watch has so few buttons, with only the Ultra model getting an additional action button. With this in mind, I think removing the double-click gesture from one of the buttons is a mistake.

Double-clicking the side button below the digital crown still retains its original function: opening cards in Apple Wallet. Hopefully, the official version of watchOS 27 can restore the same gesture to the digital crown, or at least bring it back in watchOS 27.1.

Do you use this gesture on your Apple Watch? Have you missed it in the watchOS 27 beta? Will you find it inconvenient after upgrading? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
